Title: Patrologiae graecae tomus CXLVII: Niceph. Callistus. Maximus Planudes. Callisti duo. Nicephorus Monachus. Nicephori Callisti Xanthopuli Ecclesiasticae historiae libri XVIII; accedunt Maximi Planudae, Callisti et Ignatii, Callisti Cataphugiotae, Nicephori Monachi scripta varii argumenti. Nicephori Callisti tomus tertius, caeterorum tomus unicus
Creator: Nikephoros Kallistos Xanthopoulos (church history); Maximos Planoudes; Kallistos and Ignatios Xanthopouloi; the patriarch Kallistos; Kallistos Telikoudes; Kallistos Katafygiotes; Nikephoros the Monk; Greek with parallel Latin, edited by J.-P. Migne
Publisher: Paris: J.-P. Migne (Petit-Montrouge), Patrologiae cursus completus, Series graeca, tomus 147
Publication Date: 1865
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the first title page reads '1865' and the second '1863' in this scan's OCR (file lines 200 and 262); host record: date 1857 (the series start), possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.
Language: grc (Greek with parallel or following Latin translation; the Latin and Greek share the OCR file; see the content note)
Source: Internet Archive item patrologicursus46migngoog (archive.org/details/patrologicursus46migngoog), full-text file patrologicursus46migngoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows it unchanged. Nothing was stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped (the long s glyph occurs 0 times and was left as found). The Google Books boilerplate page at the head of the OCR is left in place. The OCR text that follows is 2642464 bytes, 1944823 characters and 54508 lines. OCR quality sampled at the title pages and at about 5%, 50% and 95% of the file (lines 2738, 27267 and 51795): Greek polytonic readable with occasional slips; Latin clean.
Content note: Only a part of this volume belongs to the hesychast world. The first and larger part is the end of Nikephoros Kallistos's Ecclesiastical History (a history of the early church, not of the fourteenth century). The hesychast tracts follow, as the volume's own ELENCHUS lists them: Kallistos and Ignatios Xanthopouloi, Methodus et regula (from file line 28911); the patriarch Kallistos, Capitula de precatione; Kallistos Telikoudes, capita on quiet and selected sayings on prayer and attention (from line 32544); Kallistos Katafygiotes, on union with God and the contemplative life (from 33349); and Nikephoros the Monk, Tractatus de sobrietate et cordis custodia (from 38202). Maximos Planoudes follows, with his syllogisms on the procession of the Holy Spirit against the Latins.
